{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On the first day of autumn, Milo found a tiny brass key lodged between the boards of the old pier. It was tied to a faded green ribbon, and a paper tag bore three words: “Ask the lighthouse keeper.”

The lighthouse had been closed for years, but its keeper, Mrs. Vale, still lived in the cottage nearby. When Milo showed her the key, she smiled as if she had been expecting it. She led him up the narrow spiral stairs and unlocked a cabinet beneath the lantern room.

Inside sat a wooden music box. Its painted lid showed a ship sailing toward a crescent moon. Mrs. Vale explained that her brother had made it long ago, before he left to work on a vessel across the ocean. He had promised to return and hear the music again, but the ship never came back.

Milo carefully wound the small handle. A gentle tune rose into the room, mingling with the wind beyond the windows. Mrs. Vale closed her eyes, and for a moment the years seemed to fall away.

“Would you like to keep the key?” she asked.

Milo shook his head. “It belongs with the box.”

Instead, he asked if he could bring the music box to the harbor festival. Mrs. Vale agreed. That evening, she placed it on a table beside photographs of her brother, and Milo turned the handle while the crowd gathered around.

Afterward, a sailor visiting from another town recognized the ship in one photograph. He had heard stories from his own father about a crew member who carried a wooden music box.

Mrs. Vale listened closely as he promised to write to his family. The old tune played once more, filling the harbor with hope."}
